name: Single Permit / EU Blue Card

requirements.blocker_text: A third-country national authorised to work in Belgium for more than 90 days must also obtain authorisation to reside for more than 90 days -- the two are linked via the single permit procedure. Work authorisation is applied for through the competent REGIONAL authority (Flanders, Brussels, or Wallonia each run their own procedure), not a single federal one.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a job offer from a Belgian employer.

requirements.blocker_text: Minimum salary thresholds for highly-skilled workers are set REGIONALLY and revised annually: Flanders EUR 47,500 (from 2 August 2026, up from EUR 45,420), Brussels EUR 44,441 (2025 level maintained into 2026), Wallonia EUR 53,220 (from January 2026). The EU Blue Card threshold is EUR 63,300 nationally.

evidence_required.document: Proof of qualifications/salary meeting the applicable regional threshold

outcome.duration_length: tied to the single permit's validity period, matching the authorised employment

sources.title: IBZ -- Work (third-country nationals): work authorisation for stays over 90 days is a REGIONAL competence, paired with the federal single-permit residence authorisation

VisasUpdate -- Flanders Raises Highly-Skilled Single Permit Salary Threshold to EUR 47,500 for 2026: also cites Brussels (EUR 44,441), Wallonia (EUR 53,220), and the national EU Blue Card threshold (EUR 63,300)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Belgium). STATUS: DRAFT -- Belgium's federal structure means work-permit salary thresholds are genuinely set REGIONALLY (Flanders, Brussels, Wallonia each publish their own annual figures) rather than nationally, which the tier-1 dofi.ibz.be source confirms structurally but does not itself state in euro figures; the specific numbers are tier-3 sourced from an immigration-news aggregator. Modeled the lowest of the three 2026 regional figures (Brussels, EUR 44,441) as the baseline hard requirement, with the higher Flanders/Wallonia figures and the separate EU Blue Card threshold disclosed in blocker_text. This regional fragmentation is structurally different from every other EU country built in this dataset so far, where a single national salary threshold applies.
